name: The Bone Parish
description:
The Bone Parish is a gang of about ten augment strippers who operate in Detroit with a disturbing specialty: they harvest augments from the dead. Graveyards, morgues, disaster sites, combat zones — anywhere bodies accumulate, the Bone Parish appears. They're not fighters or kidnappers like the Skinners in Cleveland. They're ghouls. They dig up the recently buried, bribe morgue attendants, and follow the sound of gunfire to collect the freshly killed before anyone else can claim the chrome.

The crew is tiny but efficient. Ten members with a clear division of labor: two scouts who track deaths and burials, three extraction technicians who remove augments, two logistics handlers who transport and store the harvest, and three salespeople who move the product through black-market channels. They operate out of a condemned funeral home in Detroit's East English Village — a location chosen for its macabre appropriateness and its ready access to embalming chemicals that help preserve extracted augments.

The Bone Parish occupies a unique ecological niche. Their supply is consistent — people with augments die every day — and their overhead is low because their donors don't fight back. The augments they recover are often in better condition than what the Skinners pull from living victims, because the Parish takes its time and doesn't have to work around a struggling patient. They've developed a reputation for quality product, which generates steady business from chop shops and gray-market clinics.

Everyone despises them. Even criminals who deal in stolen augments find the Bone Parish distasteful. The crew doesn't care. They've embraced the revulsion as a form of protection — nobody wants to be associated with them, which means nobody pays close attention to their movements.
ideology: The dead don't need chrome. The Bone Parish frames their work as recycling — returning valuable technology to circulation rather than letting it rot underground. This is self-serving rationalization and they know it, but it's enough to let them sleep at night. Barely.
territory: Detroit's East English Village, centered on a condemned funeral home. Operational range covers all of Detroit and extends to Cleveland and Chicago for major recovery opportunities.
methods: Grave recovery — exhuming recently buried augmented individuals to harvest their cyberware
Morgue access — bribing attendants and staff for access to augmented corpses before processing
Combat trailing — following the aftermath of violence to harvest augments from casualties
Technical extraction — careful removal of augments from deceased donors using proper surgical technique
Preservation — using embalming chemicals and specialized storage to maintain augment quality
Black-market sales — moving harvested augments through established underground channels
resources: Ten specialized members with clearly defined operational roles
A condemned funeral home with preservation equipment and surgical facilities
Relationships with morgue staff, cemetery workers, and disaster responders across Detroit
Embalming chemicals and preservation compounds for augment storage
Black-market distribution network for harvested cyberware
Social invisibility — nobody watches the people who deal with the dead

relationships.reason: Both harvest and traffic augmentation components; territorial overlap in Detroit has produced violence

relationships.name: The Reclaimed
relationships.reason: The Parish operates in Detroit's ruins belt, which the Reclaimed consider their sovereign territory

relationships.name: The Gauze
relationships.reason: Medical supply relationship — the Gauze acquires surgical materials from the Parish; neither discusses provenance

relationships.name: The Ferment
relationships.reason: The Ferment provides biochemical compounds for Parish surgical operations

story_hooks: The Bone Parish harvested an augment from a corpse that wasn't quite dead — the donor survived and wants their chrome back
A funeral home recovery uncovered a body with augments that contain encrypted data — someone powerful wants that data and knows the Parish took it
The Parish is being hired to stage deaths so that specific augments can be 'recovered' from living people who want to disappear
A mass casualty event created a harvest opportunity so large that multiple factions are competing for the chrome — and the Parish was there first
One of the Parish's regular morgue contacts has been feeding them bodies that were murdered specifically for their augments — the Parish is now complicit in a killing operation
related_entities: Tethered Orbital Reconnaissance and Suppression Drone TORSD-7 'Kitestring'

known_members.name: Saint Vex
known_members.notes: The honorific 'Saint' is ironic in origin and genuine in current usage — the Bone Parish gives it to leaders who survive long enough that longevity itself becomes a credential. Vex has led the Parish for nine years, which is approximately six years longer than any prior leader. The reason for this is not charisma or ideology but a specific quality that Parish members describe as 'sees it coming' — an apparent ability to anticipate threat before it materializes that has kept her alive through circumstances that should not have permitted survival. She is 34 and she has more cyberware than flesh in her left arm and she has never asked for anything that wasn't already hers.

known_members.name: The Carpenter
known_members.notes: The Parish's internal modification specialist. Operates from a clinic space in a disused elevator machine room. No formal medical training. Seventeen years of practice. The work is competent to the degree that it has to be — in a community that cannot access licensed clinics without documentation, competence is survival. The Carpenter has refused to work on modification requests that she considers structurally dangerous regardless of payment, which has caused conflict twice and saved lives more times than that.

known_members.name: Forty
known_members.notes: Named for the caliber, not the age. 27. Has worked for the Parish since 14. The role of enforcer in the Bone Parish is not primarily violence — it is the credible suggestion of violence sufficient that violence doesn't happen, and Forty is exceptionally good at the suggestion. Has been in three firefights in thirteen years of enforcement work. This is considered unusually few. The reason is that Forty listens before anything else and most situations, given time to be understood, do not require the thing they initially appeared to require.
